summary: No held position had its thesis broken by news on 10-27. The only trade, MSM, had its results event cleared (8-K 2.02 and 10-K filed 10-22, next estimate 2027-01-06), and its only headline was Barclays raising its PT to $159 on 10-26. Today's tape was macro-driven: the Fed began a two-day meeting, tech and AI-bubble worries continued, and defensives and ETFs were the story. Position-specific newsflow was thin: DPZ got a DA Davidson PT cut ($382 from $423, Buy kept), WMT got valuation talk (Burry may trim) plus routine retail press releases, KR got an Evercore Buy at $70, VRSN had no new news beyond Wedbush's $367 PT, and MSCI (-2.6% today) had only a PT nudge from Redburn ($680) and a note on new index exclusion rules, with no headline that explains the move. Of the L2 open items, RRC was overtaken by the EQT all-stock deal (8-K 1.01 filed 10-26), SMG now has a company-confirmed Q4 date of 11-04, and the WMT 8-K 8.01 from 10-23 is still unread (I only see item numbers, not the filing text). I did not follow L2's rule to read the filings themselves; the role limits me to the news input.
upcoming: Fed decision 10-28 (two-day meeting began 10-27): two-way duration risk for BND and IEF, and an equity-beta risk for VOO, VTI and the stock book. Three mega-cap reports this week (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon; about 36% of S&P 500 earnings) bear on the AI-complex thread that has been running since 10-20. AAPL is uncertain: the file estimate is 10-29, and Benzinga earlier cited 11-02; AAPL is not held, but it moves QQQ and VOO. New this week: the iPhone Duo display-crack replacement program and the 10-27 MacBook Pro and iMac M6 launch. Held names with an estimated print: IDXX 11-02, which is about 5 trading days out (approximate, estimate is last year + 364 days); CARG 11-05; none of the other held names has an earnings date inside 5 trading days (KR 12-03, WMT 11-19, DPZ 2027-02-22, FAST 2027-01-19, MSCI and VRSN already reported, MSM 2027-01-06). The MSCI file estimate of 10-27 is stale (reported 10-20) and the SMG 5.02 detail remains unread. Shadow-book context: CART is a live takeover story (DoorDash in advanced talks for about $17B, a deal 'as soon as this week' per WSJ; 8-K 2.05 filed 10-26 for the Caper Cart wind-down of $55M-$80M charges, with Q3 earnings reported as 11-04 by Benzinga against the file's 11-09). The shadow book sold CART at $60.08 and RRC at $56.38 (merger-arb, tied to EQT), so both are worth watching for what that exit cost or saved. BTC: no exchange failure or adverse regulation (Ripple trust bank approval is constructive), but ETF outflows, Strategy pausing purchases, and a possible $72k-$76k test keep the downside narrative live; the position is -3.6% against a 10% invalidation. Most BTC headlines today are opinion or prediction-market items and carry no information.
